ruling.recommended_action: Issue a voucher refund of $7.09 to the rider (RydeTAXI meter overcharge for the 5.03 km non-exempt off-route segment at $1.4101/km, per NS-7), and remind the driver that a "take whichever way is faster" agreement covers a route to the destination, not a 1391 m excursion off the optimal corridor (RD-1/RD-5).
ruling.reasoning:
RydeTAXI metered trip, so distance feeds the meter and the calculation sits under RD-2's RydeTAXI head [F7][RD-2]. Code settles the off-route segment: 13:07–13:19, 7.41 km where the optimal route covers 2.38 km, +5.03 km, up to 1391 m off the optimal route, with no RD-4 incident on the replaced stretch [F3][F15][RD-1][RD-4].

The RD-4 screen fails: F15 records no qualifying incident on the replaced optimal stretch, and F12 (Ayer Rajah Expressway band 2, 12:41–13:07) is band evidence only, which RD-4(b) says cannot exempt a segment alone; a longer way that took 48.3 min against a 33.6 min estimate shows the reroute was not the faster way it needed to be [F12][F13][F15][F2][RD-4].

Consent (RD-5): the only rider message is F9, 13:04 — before the 13:07:15 segment start — "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late", a general route choice; the chat record is complete and timestamped, so the timing test is met [F8][F9][F10][F3][RD-5]. A general authorisation covers a route chosen to get to Suntec City, not an errand of the driver's own, a stop away from the route, or a loop that reaches nothing — and a loop that strays 1391 m off the optimal corridor while running 14.7 min over the estimate is not a destination route, so the segment is not covered by the authorisation [F3][F1][F2][RD-5]. The driver's after-trip statement that the rider agreed verbally is a claim, not consent [F11][G11].

Amount from the fare record's own rate: $42.36 ÷ 30.04 km = $1.4101/km [F7][F4][RD-2]. RD-2 refunds only the non-exempt segment's extra_km, not corridor/matching mileage inside the 200 m band, so the billed 5.59 km excess-distance line is not the refundable measure; the segment's extra_km is 5.03 km. 5.03 km × $1.4101/km = $7.0928 → $7.09. Metered waiting ($0.11) stays with the driver under RD-3(c) and the platform fee ($1.47) is a published item [F5][F7][RD-3][FARE-1].

No flag: RD-6 needs route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 and F18 shows 0 upheld, so the breach is not "repeated" [F18][RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's own message F9, sent 13:04 (before the 13:07:15 segment start) and part of a complete, fully timestamped chat record [F10], is a GENERAL route choice — 'Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late' — made in direct response to the driver's 13:03 proposal to avoid building traffic on Ayer Rajah Expressway [F8]; under RD-5 kind (1) a general 'whichever is faster' authorisation covers the routing chosen to reach the destination, and nothing in the record shows a stop or errand of the driver's own on this segment (no stop measured; the driver statement F11 adds nothing beyond the quoted message) [F3][F11][RD-5]. No RD-4 incident supports the segment on its own (band evidence only), so the exemption rests on the rider's own pre-segment authorisation, not on reasonable cause [F12][F15][RD-4].

rejected_claims.reason: Accepted that the 13:07–13:19 stretch is an off-route segment under RD-1, but it is not refundable: the rider's own pre-segment message F9 is a general 'whichever way is faster' authorisation under RD-5 and no stop or errand of the driver's own appears in the record, so the segment is exempt [F3][F9][F10][RD-1][RD-5].

The +5.6 km / +23% and +14.7 min figures are correct, but a general route authorisation is not defeated by the route turning out slower; the deviation was consented to before it began and RD-2 refunds no mileage where no unexempted segment remains [F1][F2][F9][F3][RD-2][RD-5].

The rider's reading of F9 as a general authorisation is right, but its claimed consequence is not: RD-5 kind (1) covers the routing chosen to reach the destination, and nothing in the record shows a driver's own stop or errand on this segment, so the segment is exempt rather than unexempted [F9][F8][F3][RD-5].

The named-road rule does not bite: the driver runs no '走 X 路' case, so the absence of a road-name tie between F3 and a named road is irrelevant; the operative consent is the general authorisation in F9 [F9][F8][F3][RD-5].
Correct that F11 is a claim and not consent, but it is not needed: the consent relied on is the rider's own timestamped F9, read by its words [F9][F11][F3][RD-5][G11].

Accepted that no RD-4(a)/(b) exemption arises (F15 records no incident; band evidence alone does not exempt), but the segment is nonetheless exempt under RD-5 on the rider's own authorisation, so the conclusion that it is unexempted does not follow [F12][F15][F9][RD-4][RD-5].

The excess-distance line is $7.88 as billed (5.59 km × $1.4101/km) but RD-2 refunds only non-exempt segment extra_km, and here the only segment is exempt, so the refundable sum is $0 and the claim for $7.88 fails [F4][F3][F9][RD-2][RD-5].
Correct that the metered waiting of $0.11 is not refundable under RD-3(c)/RD-2; the rider does not claim it and it stays charged [F5][RD-3][RD-2].
Correct: F18 shows 0 upheld route disputes, so RD-6's 'repeated' predicate (route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1) is not met and no flag_account is sought [F18][RD-6].

The congestion account does not itself exempt the segment — F12 is band evidence only and F15 records no incident, so under RD-4(b) the band record alone cannot carry an exemption; the segment is exempt on the rider's RD-5 authorisation instead [F12][F13][F15][RD-4][RD-5].

Accepted that no exemption arises under RD-4(a) or (b); the driver's concession that no incident supports the reroute is right, and the exemption here comes from F9 under RD-5 [F12][F15][F9][RD-4][RD-5].

The arithmetic (5.59 km × $1.4101/km = $7.88) is right, but it is not payable: RD-2 only refunds unexempted segments and the single segment is exempt, so nothing is refundable; the platform fee and metered waiting remain charged [F4][F3][F5][F7][RD-2][RD-3][FARE-1].
